question: In the BatPaC comparison, how much lower are the total pack cost and the material cost with Co-free cathodes than with NCA cathodes?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%BatPaC%' OR text ILIKE '%pack cost%' OR text ILIKE '%material cost%' OR text ILIKE '%NCA%' ORDER BY page, id
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE id IN ('p3.L15','p3.L16','p3.L17','p3.L18','p3.L19','p3.L20','p3.L21') ORDER BY id

SELECT
 CAST(replace(regexp_extract(n1.text,'\$([0-9 ]+) total pack',1),' ','') AS INT) - CAST(regexp_extract(f1.text,'\(\$([0-9]+) total pack',1) AS INT) AS total_pack_diff,
 CAST(regexp_extract(n2.text,'\$([0-9]+) material cost',1) AS INT) - CAST(regexp_extract(f1.text,'\$([0-9]+) material costs',1) AS INT) AS material_diff
FROM lines f1, lines n1, lines n2
WHERE f1.id='p3.L18' AND n1.id='p3.L19' AND n2.id='p3.L20'

rendered: In the BatPaC comparison (Fig. 2[1]), the Co-free cathode system is projected at $8500 total pack cost[2] with $3500 material costs[3], versus $10 000 total pack[4] and $5000 material cost[5] for the NCA system. Total pack cost is therefore lower with Co-free cathodes by 1500[6] dollars per pack, and material cost is lower by 1500[7] dollars per pack.

source.label: Fig. 2
source.caption: Figure 2. Potential of Co-free cathode materials for low-cost LIBs. Cost projections are based on producing 1 million EVs with a 200 mile range powered by 58.8 kWh LIB packs.
